name: Garrison or transport
summary: A vehicle or building with seats that teammates enter to travel or shelter protected, and leave where they choose. In a vehicle the riders can't fight while inside, and the carrier often has a weak gun or none, so its worth lies in moving the team: rushing an objective, crossing water or cliffs, slipping past defences, or pulling the hurt out of a fight. Versions differ in how many seats there are, what can ride (soldiers only, or a vehicle slung underneath), how fast riders get in and out, whether the carrier can drop them from the air, and what happens to them when it dies. A building or bunker garrison belongs here even when its riders fire out of it. A vehicle whose riders fire out or set its weapon is passenger-sets-weapon, and respawning teammates inside it is host-spawn-point.
counterplay: Catch it loaded: one anti-armour burst on a full carrier puts several players out of the fight at once, thrown out hurt and on foot.
Cover the exits: riders come out in a short stagger beside the carrier, so splash and pre-aimed fire catch them as they unload.
Count the seats: the carrier shows how many ride inside, so you know how big the drop will be before it lands.
Hit fliers while they hover low and still to load or unload; that is when dropships are easiest to shoot.
Spot it early and block its route: fixed defences alone don't stop a carrier that drives past them.
Clear a garrison with fire, gas, flash-bangs or long-range artillery rather than charging its walls.

other_examples.note: Carries five infantry under the ground, unseen except by a sensor array, and comes up beside its target, so players fill it with engineers to surface next to enemy buildings and capture them. It can't go under or come up through concrete paving, Tiberium fields or uneven ground, and it has no weapon of its own.

An attack and transport helicopter that lifts either a squad of soldiers or one light or medium vehicle slung beneath it, never both at once, and drops them with an evacuate order. It lets Soviet players leapfrog tanks forward or hit a base from an unexpected side, but with its guns pointed at the ground and precious cargo aboard it is easy prey for fighters.

A heavy bomber that can take five infantry aboard while landed and, on a button, drops them all at once by parachute behind enemy lines. The riders die if it is shot down with them still aboard, and the bomber is vulnerable to anti-air.

other_examples.unit: Garrisoning buildings (Red Alert 2, Generals and Zero Hour)
other_examples.note: Infantry enter civilian buildings or built bunkers and fight from inside. In Generals the building takes the damage instead of the soldiers until it is badly hurt, then throws them out at half health; garrisoned soldiers can't be ordered about or use their special abilities. Answers include flash-bang grenades, rangers rappelling in from a helicopter, microwave, flame or toxin weapons that kill the occupants, bunker-busting bombs, and artillery that outranges the building. Some network buildings hold vehicles too and heal what is inside, but nothing fires out of them.

A dropship that also heals infantry. It scoops units up almost instantly, quickly enough to save them from incoming shots, but lets them out one at a time with a short gap between each, and it is most exposed while unloading. A single heavy walker fills it entirely, and a short engine boost makes it fast in and out.

A built garrison for four infantry, or fewer when larger soldiers take two places. Inside they can't be hurt and those with guns shoot out with a little extra reach; in the first game they can't use abilities inside and walk out unharmed when the bunker falls. Only terran infantry may enter.

An armoured carrier for two infantry squads (Seraphim excepted) with its own storm bolter. Players use it to drop troops near the front, and above all to rush melee squads into contact before the enemy can pull back.

sources.title: Soulstorm/Rhino transport, Dawn of War Wiki

other_examples.note: Carries up to three squads at more than twice walking pace, protected from fire, and can stay nearby to top up squads with fresh men. Its roof machine gun is manned only while someone rides inside and is no real weapon, so the guide's advice is to unload when firepower is needed. An upgrade swaps the troop bay for a quad anti-aircraft mount, turning it into a fighting vehicle that can no longer carry anyone.

sources.title: M3 Halftrack, Company of Heroes Wiki

other_examples.note: Air transports carry land units, tanks included, to drop them behind the enemy, over water or up cliffs, or to pull the commander out of danger; bigger transports carry more and heavier units. Units must stand still while they are loaded and unloaded. A ferry order sets up a standing route that carries anything sent to its start beacon to the far end.

shooter_analogues.note: A slow, very tough dropship with a pilot, four gunners and seven passenger seats. Squad members can spawn into it, and its ejection system cancels a rider's speed and briefly protects them from falling damage, so a full squad can jump out over a base: the hot drop.

A driver and five passengers who can do nothing while they ride; the truck has no weapon. Besides people it hauls crates and tows field guns and trailers, and it is fragile, so drivers carry a rifle and watch the roads for raiders.

A player-driven carrier with four seats; the driver steers and fires its machine gun. In multiplayer it is the usual way to rush the enemy base, early or late in a match, and it cuts down lone soldiers and light vehicles on the way.

sources.title: GDI armored personnel carrier (Renegade), Command & Conquer Wiki

shooter_analogues.note: The main ground transport: a driver, two gunners and nine passengers. For contrast, its deployed mode, a mobile spawn station, belongs to host-spawn-point.

For contrast (passenger-sets-weapon, fire-ports variant): a pilot, two door gunners and two passengers who use their own kit from the cabin, so an engineer can repair the helicopter in flight or fire launchers out of it. In Battlefield 4 anyone on the team can spawn into it.

player_translation.summary: A fast, armoured carrier whose driver's job is moving the team: two to four teammates hop in with E, ride protected while they look out, ping and pick an exit, and pile out together where the driver parks. If the carrier dies, everyone inside is thrown out hurt.
as_user: As the driver you buy a quick, tough chassis with two to four seats and little or no weapon of its own; your value is the people you move.
Teammates load with E next to you and can leave with E at any time; you unload everyone with G, so you decide where the team lands.
Your skill is routing and timing: paths that avoid anti-armour, a parking spot behind cover, and a drop that lands with your team's push.
As a rider you trade a few seconds of not fighting for speed and safety. You look out with a wider view, ping targets and choose the side you will get out on.
If the carrier dies, everyone inside is thrown out hurt, so a loaded carrier caught in the open is a disaster: that is the tension.
as_target: Seat pips on the carrier's nameplate show how many ride inside, so you know what is coming.
Kill it before it unloads: anti-armour on a loaded carrier throws several players out hurt at once, and splash catches them as they spill out.
Watch where it parks: riders come out of its doors in a short stagger, so pre-aim the exits.
Turrets and fixed defences won't stop it; answer carriers with mobile anti-armour and early spotting.
teammates: A driver-and-squad combo: 'need a ride' pings, regrouping after respawn, and one coordinated drop on an objective.
Escorts keep anti-armour off the carrier, and the carrier repays them by pulling hurt teammates out of fights.
The other team needs spotters and mobile anti-armour to catch it on the move.
The driver earns an assist for kills its riders make shortly after it drops them, so driving pays.
controls: The base pattern is passive and spends no counted key: E enters the nearest free seat or leaves it, 1-3 switch seats, hold X bails out, G unloads every rider at once (it is also the evict key, so it has a short cooldown against griefing), and middle mouse pings 'need a ride' or 'pick me up'.
Driver: WASD to move and the mouse to aim any weapon the chassis has; seats can be locked from the vehicle menu.
Rider: the mouse moves a look-out camera around the carrier and picks the exit side; left mouse pings what is under the cursor.
Variants that need a counted key put it on Q: dropping riders from the air, hooking a teammate's vehicle, or hitching a tow.
feedback: Seat pips on the nameplate for everyone (filled for a rider), and the riders' class icons for the carrier's own team.
A door sound and animation when someone gets in or out, and a short stagger between riders leaving, so an unload reads as several bodies coming out.
Rider HUD: the carrier's outline and health, the chosen exit side, and a bail-out prompt when the hull is low.
Driver HUD: who is aboard and their health, and a warning when anti-armour locks on.
When it dies: a loud blast, riders tumbling out with a stun ring, and a kill feed line that names everyone thrown out.
changes_from_rts: RTS riders are units that wait patiently; players won't sit idle for long, so trips must be short, the view from inside useful (look out, ping, pick an exit) and the payoff on arrival big.

Red Alert 3's Sudden Transport and Century Bomber kill their riders with them, a penalty on several people for one driver's mistake; here riders are thrown out hurt, as in the passenger-sets-weapon pattern.
Anti-grief rules: riders can always leave (E) or bail out (X), and drivers can evict (G) on a cooldown or lock seats from the vehicle menu.
Capacity follows team size, two to four seats rather than five or twelve; a soldier takes one seat and a power suit two.
Loading is quick and unloading is staggered, so a full unload is visible to the enemy but not slow.

Respawning inside a carrier is host-spawn-point and firing out of it is passenger-sets-weapon, so the base carrier does neither; building garrisons become a feature of map buildings, since cards are units.

team_play.notes: All of its value comes from teammates: the driver ferries and evacuates them, and the riders repay it by escorting it and making the drop count. The other team must spot it early and keep anti-armour ready.

notes: Rides on the seat system that every vehicle needs anyway: enter, leave, switch seat, bail out and evict are universal keys.
Riders need a look-out camera, exits placed on open ground beside the carrier, and ejection when it dies.
Several players in one networked vehicle: the carrier's movement must stay smooth for every rider's camera.
Variants add work: slinging a vehicle under an aircraft (attachment and physics), a safe-fall state for drops from the air, and the burrow layer for tunnelling.
A fast carrier can land several players on a backline or objective before anyone reacts; seat pips and spotting must give warning.
Riders who could heal or shoot freely while protected would make an armoured carrier unkillable in a choke, so riders do neither in the base pattern.
Killing riders with the carrier, as Red Alert 3 does, punishes several players for one mistake; throwing them out hurt keeps the drama without the wipe.
Airlifting heavy vehicles moves the slowest, strongest units around too freely; keep the lift slow and fragile.
Everyone must see how many ride inside, and its own team who they are.
Unloads must be visible and staggered, or a full squad seems to appear from nowhere.
Carriers whose riders fire out (passenger-sets-weapon) must look different from cargo carriers.

variants.name: Armoured carrier
variants.summary: A ground or hover carrier with a few seats: riders are protected and can't act until they get out, and they all leave at once where it stops.
variants.seen_in: Red Alert 3 Sudden Transport and Riptide ACV, Renegade APC, Foxhole trucks, Dawn of War Rhino

variants.name: Dropship
variants.summary: A flying carrier that lifts riders over walls, water and cliffs and sets them down; it must hover low and still to load and unload, which is when it is easiest to hit.
variants.seen_in: StarCraft II Medivac, Supreme Commander air transports, PlanetSide 2 Galaxy, Red Alert 3 Twinblade

countered_by.why: Anti-air shoots it down with its riders aboard, most easily while it hovers to load or unload.

variants.name: Hot drop
variants.summary: On Q, every rider is thrown out over a spot with a slowed, safe fall, so they land spread out and briefly exposed while the carrier never has to touch down.
variants.seen_in: Red Alert 3 Century Bomber Paradrop, PlanetSide 2 Galaxy ejection system

countered_by.why: Anti-air downs it before the drop, and splash catches the riders while they fall.

variants.name: Quick lift
variants.summary: Picking a teammate up is near-instant while letting riders out is staggered, so a well-timed pickup saves a teammate from a lethal shot.

variants.name: Field hospital
variants.summary: Riders slowly regain health while inside, so the carrier doubles as a safe place to recover between pushes.
variants.seen_in: An original twist on StarCraft II's healing Medivac; Generals tunnel networks heal the units inside them

variants.name: Airlift a vehicle
variants.summary: Instead of soldiers, it hooks one teammate's vehicle with its driver aboard and flies it elsewhere; it carries troops or a vehicle, never both, and while hauling it is slow and easy prey.
variants.seen_in: Red Alert 3 Twinblade, StarCraft II Medivac lifting a Thor, Supreme Commander air transports

countered_by.why: Slowed by its load, it is easy prey for anti-air.

variants.name: Tow hook
variants.summary: Hitch a teammate's slow field gun or crippled vehicle behind you and drag it into position; the towed teammate can't drive until unhitched.

adds_strengths.why: Drags a slow teammate's gun or a crippled vehicle into place far faster than it could move itself.

adds_weaknesses.why: While towing it is slow and turns badly, and the towed teammate can't move on their own.

variants.name: Tunnel carrier
variants.summary: Riders travel under the ground with the carrier, unseen, and come up beside the target; hard floors and water stop it surfacing.

adds_strengths.why: Moves several teammates faster than they walk, protected inside, and puts them down where the team needs them.

adds_weaknesses.why: Riders can't fight from inside, so a loaded carrier caught in the open takes several players out of the fight, and if it dies they are thrown out hurt.

counters.why: Carries a strike team past turrets and fixed defences and unloads it behind them.

countered_by.why: A loaded carrier is a prize: killing it throws every rider out hurt at once.
Splash catches the riders as they spill out together.

open_questions: What can riders do inside: nothing (the RTS rule), look out and ping (used in this file), or also heal slowly?
Do riders die with the carrier, as in Red Alert 3, or get thrown out hurt? (Recommended, and used here: thrown out hurt.)
How many seats per tier, given the team size?
Should a carrier be able to lift or tow a teammate's vehicle at all, given that the teammate loses control while hauled?
Should enemies see the exact seat count, or only that the carrier is loaded?

shooter_fit.reason: Transports are a staple of team shooters (Battlefield, PlanetSide 2, Renegade, Foxhole) and give a driver a team job; riders who can't act need short trips and a strong payoff when they arrive.

review.notes: Re-checked field by field against its sources by the batch r1 checker, which covered all 33 batch patterns; research/r1/checker/checks.json lists every field and verdict. The wrong paths were fixed as the skeptic confirmed (cbe6de8).
